## Current position

M3 remains in progress. The final monotone transport ensembles meet the agreed held-out
accuracy target ([MAST-U: Q_e 17.8%, Q_i 25.2%; ITER: Q_e 7.2%, Q_i 10.8%; all meet the 30% target]{.claim}[C-129](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-129){.cid .st-measured}). Local derivative, fallback and conservation checks
cover RAPTOR L-mode and ITER hybrid ([15 gradient, JIT, fallback and discrete-balance checks pass across RAPTOR and ITER hybrid in each mode]{.claim}[C-146](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-146){.cid .st-tested}). The ITER hybrid derivative checks
use an explicit Newton solver override; the existing linear-solver timing scenario is separate.

Guards, grouped response datasets and a baseline trainer are built for radio-frequency (RF) and pedestal
responses. Their software checks use synthetic numerical fixtures
([25 synthetic contract tests pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-143](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-143){.cid .st-tested}, [26 synthetic baseline-pipeline tests pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-145](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-145){.cid .st-tested}). No new RF or pedestal model is trained.
The owner-selected pretrained ITER pedestal model now has a JAX port with numeric checks
([12 upstream scalar regression values agree within relative tolerance 1e-12]{.claim}[C-149](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-149){.cid .st-measured}, [12 focused tests pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-150](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-150){.cid .st-tested}); coupled acceptance remains unfinished.
Final-model matched speed-up remains unmeasured.

## Complete the performance comparison {#performance}

Resolve the cancelled compute run, then agree a fresh bounded submission. Compare TGLF,
the final monotone surrogate and QLKNN using matched scenario, grid and solver settings.
Record compilation separately from execution, resource allocation, finite profiles, solver
status, profile errors and accepted-state guard rejection. Every output carries provenance.

Profile Newton separately to distinguish ensemble inference, transport/geometry work and
Jacobian construction. Keep unresolved overlap visible ([K-022](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-022)). Historical speed-up belongs
to the original model; timings from different hosts or drivers cannot establish final-model
speed-up.

**Done when:** a reproducible final-model runtime comparison and discrepancy report exist,
with allocation and solver settings stated.

The expanded scheduler audit still gives no cancellation cause. A bounded replacement
request has been reviewed and awaits that explanation/remedy and fresh approval. The runner
now rejects coarse-tolerance results, records effective CPU allocation, separates warm-up
from execution and records final-state guard diagnostics after timing. Focused checks pass
([11 performance-tool checks pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-147](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-147){.cid .st-tested}). The offline saved-trace audit records unresolved component attribution
([72059 complete HLO events with about 5.369 s of covered trace time]{.claim}[C-148](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-148){.cid .st-preliminary}); [K-022](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-022) remains open. Draft entry 28 is in the private review copy.

remains, with predictive closure deferred; IC is deferred.

Complete the EC launch/current-drive prescription, power convention and coordinate/units

The native EC output reader preserves separate channels and SI units; its focused

logs and failures; its combined checks pass ([40 focused pilot, reader and Tier A checks pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-153](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-153){.cid .st-tested}). The external
reference now builds with a replacement plotting library ([one external reference executable builds with verified artifacts and resolved runtime libraries]{.claim}[C-154](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-154){.cid .st-measured}).
The corrected numerical pilot is complete with readable native profiles
([the corrected EC reference completes in 83.16 s with readable native profiles]{.claim}[C-156](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-156){.cid .st-measured}). Native accounting and descriptive saved-reference
comparison are retained; the rendered PostScript page is blank. Settle the
production coupling contracts and grouped sampling before reviewing a separate

**Done when:** those contracts and required access are recorded. These workstreams can

## Train and integrate the response surrogates {#responses}

Define physically related case groups and label a small baseline. Keep entire groups together
in training and holdout sets. Inspect failed labels, sampled domains and physical integrals.
After the baseline, agree held-out accuracy metrics and targets with the owner.

Train structured EC ensembles and evaluate untouched holdouts. The selected pretrained
ITER pedestal is ported directly; no second network needs to learn its outputs. Integrate source and boundary
responses into TORAX behind guards with Tier A fallbacks. Supply channel adapters required
by the selected targets. Check gradients, finite execution, energy/particle balance, physical
rejection, fallback use and coupled cost. Pointwise profile errors alone do not establish
absorbed-power accuracy.

**Done when:** the reference datasets, checkpoints, accuracy results, guarded coupled checks
and matched cost measurements have provenance and meet the agreed criteria.

## Close M3, then start M4 {#verification}

Audit the complete M3 criteria: held-out accuracy, differentiable guarded execution and
measured end-to-end speed-up. Transport accuracy alone does not close the RF/pedestal tasks.
Keep the ion-flux convention, monotonicity departure, default-root tolerance and domain limits
visible ([K-024](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-024), [K-025](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-025), [K-026](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-026)).

After M3 acceptance, agree verification properties and trajectory tolerances with the owner.
Prove properties over declared input boxes, calibrate uncertainty on held-out data, compare
trajectories against Tier A references and prepare per-surrogate verified-domain reports.
Certification review closes M4. Sampled monotonicity and raw ensemble spread are not
certificates.

## Keep the build log current {#build-log}

milestone state and executed statistics. Counts that reuse unchanged execution reports retain
that qualification. Drafts and disclosure-held pages remain in the private review copy until
the owner reviews them. The owner renders and publishes the separate website handoff.
